What is your opinion on hunting?

I posted my opinion of hunting as a reply to someone in a different discussion, and would like to hear what other people's opinions are. Here is my opinion:

I would personally not hunt but as long as you do so responsibly, with respect and sustainably then I cannot tell you not to. I just hope there is as little suffering as possible, that the animal goes to good use and you respect nature.

I know that in some areas there is an over population of deer and this causes malnutrition and disease. Bullets are much less harmful and cause less suffering than that. (And wolves are not a good way to go, either.)
It's not bad. Sure, you're killing animals, but you're not going mass-killing-genocide-full-Hitler on them. Besides, hunting is often for food.

I don't like hunting for the sake of hunting. I can't say I totally agree with hunting for the sake of ecological conservation either, but I can see why people would want to do it. But if someone is making use of the animals they kill; effectively catching and killing their own dinner, then I don't have much of a problem with that.

So basically if you hunt for food then hey, more power to you. If you're just killing things then I don't like you.
What about hunting to protect property or crops? Crows eat corn, hogs are very destructive.
I would put that under ecological reasons. Killing pests is something I can understand too, no matter the size of the pest. It's killing something like a deer just to mount its head I can't abide.

I myself do not hunt, however a number of my family members do. I do not see any problem with hunting so long as it's done within the very clear parameters of the law. Around here, white tail deer are typically what people hunt. They are over-populated at present and cause many injuries to humans via car accidents. What I always say to people who oppose hunting is "Would you rather have someone ethically kill a deer and then take it to a butcher to feed themselves for the next few months, or would you rather hit the deer with your car, totaling your car, and have the deer carcass taken to the local incinerator?"

I hunt whitetail as well as a couple of other animals. I would like to add that not only are they hazardous on the road but with the population as high as it is, without hunting, many will die of starvation over the winter. Deer have few natural predators and a harsh winter will take a tremendous toll on the populations. Culling the herd will allow more to survive. Not only that but most hunters spend a great deal of time managing the forest they hunt. They also create food plots on their land for the deer to keep the deer around all year. This helps provide additional food for them that they wouldn't otherwise have access to. The property I hunt will remain a forest for the foreseeable future as will most of the properties around it. That habitat will continue to be managed and sustainable forever.

Hunting has sustained human life since the beginning of our existence. If you're hunting for food and utilizing every part of the animal, or selling it to someone else that they may utilize it then I see no problem with it whatsoever. It's something we've done for out entire existence, I don't understand why people are suddenly getting so butthurt about it. That being said, hunting for food, poaching, and trophy hunting are completely different things. Poachers can burn in hell. Trophy hunters tend to stimulate the economies where they practice and actually put money back towards environmental conservation, if it is done properly.

I hunt. 50% or greater of the meat my family consumes is wild game. I am not a trophy hunter, though I do enjoy getting a larger animal (more meat for my family).

We eat the meat, heart, and liver. I am going to see if I can do tongue this year. We make broth from the bones/marrow. I give the hides to a tanner. I have used the butchering process to teach my kids anatomy including dissecting the brain and eyes.

EDIT: I forgot to add: all the scraps, ears, lower leg pieces all go to 2 of my friend's dogs. Very little gets thrown away.

I'd say that I make a good effort to use everything I can.

For the tongue, try pickling it (if you liked pickled stuff, anyway). I've had pickled deer tongue before and it was actually pretty good. Sadly, I never keep the tongue in the deer I get and we stopped even looking at the livers after about a 5 year stretch where every single one of them had flukes. Heart is my favorite though.

I am repeating this post from yesterday because I do not want to retype the whole thing again today.

Hunting is very good for the world. The amount of hunting tags are not just picked out of a hat, population numbers are studied over a long period of time allowing for stable populations with hunters. The hunters replace predators that were lost when humans settled the area. The amount of space and resources that carnivores need is much larger than herbivores. In most settled spaces there is no more big game carnivores to eat larger herbivores like deer, moose, or elk.

Deer, moose, and elk are actually a HUGE problem. Not only do they cause loss of human life via car accidents, but they cause massive damage to ecosystems. Deer eat new growth which causes forests to not regenerate from damage and actually erode. They tend to push out medium sized herbivores and kill medium sized predators. Here is a fun link about reintroducing wolves back into Yellowstone park. Think of the wolves as similar to hunters. The impact of hunters is smaller but still important.

The fees that hunters pay is used to help programs to support wildlife. Very few people are deeply concerned about fringe birds or plants, but many lesser known species serve an important role in ecosystems. The fee that hunters pay towards the 'known' animals is used to support programs to help the 'unknown' animals. Further, hunters need to have high quality wildlife in order to have something to hunt. This means they happily provide a constant source of political pressure and money to keep wildlife away from industrial development and from natural decay. It also allows for more money to go into regional markets. A hunter does not only pay the fee involved in the hunt, they also pay for the gun, gear, lodging, meals, etc. All of these go into regional groups that support wildlife in some form. Economies built off of preserving nature fight very strongly to keep the land wild.

Thank you very much for this informative post. I would never be able to hunt, killing an animal would haunt me and I'd hate myself for it, but I understand it needs to be done. (It is natural that prey is hunted and killed by predators, not allowed to over-populate or grow old and become weak and diseased)

I hate that it has to be done but nature is cruel. The reintroduction of wolves is good, and I would never stand against that, but I believe hunting is actually a better solution in a lot of ways.

Wolves kill in a very cruel manner which causes a lot of pain and suffering to their prey

Wolves do not stimulate the economy as much as a hunter does (for the reasons you have listed)

Hunters are able to eat or sell the carcass of their prey, meaning that humans benefit from hunters, but not from wolves.

It is easier to control what a hunter kills and how many of that thing a hunter can kill, humans have less control over wolves. (I have no sources for this but it is my guess, we cannot easily control the spread of wildlife once we have introduced it, although we can predict it)
Hunting for food, or to cull an over populated herd, is fine. Hunting just to kill something is not.
